can-buoy.context: A flat topped cylindrical buoy with a stripe floating on wavy water. Used for channel marking, nautical charts, boating guides and harbor navigation topics.

nun-buoy.context: A cone shaped buoy with a pointed top and a band floating on water. Used for channel marking, nautical charts and boating education about lateral marks.

spar-buoy.context: A tall thin pole shaped buoy standing upright with most of its length under a wavy waterline. Used for marking shallow channels, moorings and fishing areas.

bell-buoy.context: A buoy with an open frame tower holding a bell that rings as waves rock it. Used for audible warnings, harbor approaches and nautical safety topics.

whistle-buoy.context: A buoy with a short whistle pipe on top and sound marks around it. Used for audible navigation aids, harbor approaches and fog signal topics.

mooring-buoy.context: A round ball buoy on the water with a ring on top and a chain dropping to the seabed. Used for mooring fields, anchorage guides and marina services.

isolated-danger-mark.context: A pillar buoy with a central band and two stacked spheres as its topmark. Used for charts and boating courses to show a hazard such as a wreck or rock.

safe-water-mark.context: A round striped buoy with a single sphere on a short pole. Used to show open water around a channel, in charts and boating courses.

cardinal-mark.context: A pillar buoy topped by two cones, one pointing up and one down. Used in boating courses and nautical charts to show the safe side to pass a hazard.

special-mark-buoy.context: A pillar buoy topped with a single X shaped cross. Used for marking special areas such as cables, pipelines, anchorages and recreation zones.

lobster-buoy.context: A small bullet shaped foam float with a rope trailing down from it. Used for lobster and crab fishing, trap marking and coastal fishing content.

surface-marker-buoy.context: A tall narrow inflatable tube floating upright on the water with a thin line going down. Used by scuba divers to mark their position for boats.

racing-mark-buoy.context: An inflatable pyramid shaped mark floating on the water with a line anchoring it below. Used for regattas, sailing races and sailing club course topics.

daybeacon.context: A single post standing in the water carrying a flat triangular sign board on top. Used as a fixed channel marker in shallow water, in charts and boating courses.

boat-navigation-lights.context: A boat seen from above with a lamp on each side casting a wedge of light outward. Used for night boating rules, running lights and safety courses.

ship-lantern.context: A metal lantern with a domed cap, a glass globe inside a guard and a carrying ring. Used for old sailing ships, camping, storm lamps and nautical decor.

range-lights.context: Two posts carrying lights, a short one in front and a tall one behind, standing on a shoreline. Used for leading lights that mark the safe line into a channel.

sector-light.context: A small light tower casting three fan shaped beams in different directions. Used for coastal light guides showing colored sectors and safe bearings.

screw-pile-lighthouse.context: A small cottage with a lantern on its roof standing on thin legs above the water. Used for historic offshore lights, coastal heritage and nautical history topics.

skeleton-tower-lighthouse.context: A tall open steel lattice tower that tapers upward to a small lantern room. Used for lighthouse guides, coastal navigation and maritime heritage topics.

caisson-lighthouse.context: A squat round iron base rising from the water like a spark plug, topped by a small tower and lantern. Used for offshore lighthouse and coastal history topics.

pierhead-light.context: A short tapered light tower with a pointed lamp room standing at the end of a harbor pier on posts. Used for harbor entrances and breakwater lights.

fresnel-lens.context: A beehive shaped lighthouse lens made of stacked glass rings with a base. Used for lighthouse museums, optics history and coastal light guides.

mooring-bitts.context: Two short thick posts on a shared base plate with a rope wound around them in a figure eight. Used for dock fittings, boat tie up and deck hardware guides.

fairlead-chock.context: A deck fitting with two curved horns facing each other to form a slot that guides a rope. Used for mooring hardware, deck equipment and boat parts guides.

hawsepipe.context: A ship's bow seen from the side with an anchor drawn up snug into a round opening in the hull. Used for ship parts, anchor handling and maritime vocabulary.

concrete-tetrapod.context: A chunky concrete block with four stubby legs pointing in different directions. Used for breakwaters, coastal defense and civil engineering topics.

groyne.context: A row of wooden posts topped by a plank running from the beach out into the waves. Used for coastal erosion, beach management and shoreline engineering topics.

sea-wall.context: A curved concrete wall at the shoreline with a big wave curling back off its face. Used for flood defense, coastal protection and storm surge topics.

floating-dry-dock.context: A U shaped floating pontoon with high side walls and a ship lifted inside it. Used for shipyards, ship repair and maritime industry topics.

marine-fuel-dock.context: A fuel pump with a hose standing on a wooden pier beside the water. Used for marina services, boat refueling and harbor facility maps.

shore-power-pedestal.context: A short post on a marina dock with a light on top, a socket panel and a cable running away. Used for marina amenities and boat electrical hookup.

mooring-dolphin.context: A cluster of wooden piles bound together at the top, standing in the water. Used for harbor structures, berthing guides and ship mooring topics.

boat-hook.context: A long pole with a metal tip that has a straight point and a curved hook. Used for docking, reaching mooring lines and picking up objects from the water.

boat-cradle.context: A boat hull with a small flag resting on a frame of supports and legs. Used for boatyards, winter storage and boat maintenance on land.

mooring-ring.context: A heavy iron ring hanging from a bolted plate set into the top of a stone quay wall. Used for harbor fittings and tying up boats along a wharf.

liferaft-canister.context: A capsule shaped container split along the middle and held in a cradle on a ship rail. Used for safety equipment, boat safety checks and emergency gear.

horseshoe-buoy.context: A U shaped horseshoe lifebuoy with two bands across its sides. Used for man overboard rescue, boat safety and lifesaving equipment.

boat-storage-rack.context: A tall steel rack with three levels, each holding a small boat on its shelf. Used for dry stack marinas and boat storage facilities.

dock-cart.context: A deep tub barrow on a large wheel with a long handle, used to move gear along a marina dock. Used for marina amenities and provisioning.

cargo-hand-hook.context: A short curved steel hook with a T shaped handle. Used for dockworkers and longshore workers handling sacks, bales and crates.

mooring-reel.context: A deck mounted spool with flanges on a stand, with a thick rope wound around its core. Used for winches, deck machinery and rope handling topics.

ship-cargo-derrick.context: A ship's mast with an angled boom and a cable lifting a crate from the hold. Used for cargo handling, freighters and loading gear.

container-twistlock.context: A cone shaped connector on a plate with a twist handle, used to lock shipping containers together. Used for container terminals and lashing equipment.

boat-wake.context: A small boat seen from above moving forward and leaving a V shaped trail of wake lines behind it. Used for speed, boating rules and wake surfing topics.

no-wake-zone.context: A round sign showing a small boat crossed out by a diagonal bar. Used for harbor speed limits, idle speed areas and boating regulation topics.

marlinspike.context: A long tapered steel spike with a rounded head and a small hole, set on a diagonal. Used for splicing, knot tying and traditional rope work topics.

splicing-fid.context: A smooth tapered cone with a pointed tip and a rounded base, set on a diagonal. Used for opening rope strands in splicing and rope work guides.

knot-board.context: A framed board with rows of cords, each carrying small knots. Used for sailing and scouting education, knot tying displays and nautical decor.

rope-fender.context: A pear shaped fender made of braided rope hanging from a short rope loop. Used for boat bumpers, dock protection and traditional nautical decor.

rat-guard.context: A round metal disc clamped around a diagonal mooring line running from a ship to the quay. Used for port safety, ship mooring and pest control topics.

cargo-net.context: A square net of thick rope mesh gathered at the corners onto a single lifting ring, holding a load. Used for cargo handling and dockside lifting topics.

flemish-coil.context: A rope laid flat in a tight spiral, seen from above. Used for tidy deck work, sailing seamanship and decorative rope topics.

clove-hitch.context: A horizontal pole wrapped by rope whose two turns cross in an X on the front, with the ends hanging above and below. Used for knot tutorials, scouting and sailing.

overhand-knot.context: A single rope with one simple loop crossing over itself in the middle, with the ends leaving in opposite directions. Used for knot basics and stopper knot topics.

monkey-fist-knot.context: A round ball of woven rope turns with a single rope tail coming out. Used for heaving lines, throwing weights, keychains and decorative rope work.

turks-head-knot.context: A braided rope band woven around a cylinder in a repeating over and under pattern, like a ring. Used for decorative knot work, bracelets and handle wraps.

eye-splice.context: A rope end bent back into a fixed eye loop, with its strands woven into the standing part. Used for rigging, mooring lines and rope work tutorials.

ocean-plait-mat.context: An oval flat mat woven from a single rope in a tight lattice of diamonds. Used for decorative rope work, deck mats and nautical craft topics.

rope-whipping.context: A rope end with bands of tight twine wrapped near the tip, with the strands fanning out below. Used for rope care and preventing fraying.
